searches.reason: Move from aggregate margins to intervention-based diagnosis of historical-context use. The latest padding probes pass, making matched-target prefix removal, recent-item removal and order perturbations practical next steps. Seek paired rank changes and recurrent-state or gradient measurements that distinguish useful long-term context from excessive recency dependence, without interpreting sensitivity as proof of stale intent. All probes should inspect one frozen GRU4Rec model per category.

searches.reason: Connect qualitative feedback to auditable recommendation failures. Seek evidence-linked annotation protocols that separate immediate choice, general interest, deferral, explicit mismatch and insufficient information, with agreement and abstention checks. Ownership, compatibility and intent must remain unobserved unless explicitly supported by feedback; title or description similarity alone cannot establish them. Start with the twenty training-user recommendation lists and avoid fitting another predictor.

searches.reason: Replace easy sampled-pair separation with a reproducible ranking stress test. Seek fixed causal training-prefix audits using full-catalog scoring, popularity strata and lexical hard competitors derived only from permitted titles and descriptions. Investigate which probes detect controlled failures such as ignored history or shuffled chronology, and report uncertainty and computational cost. These audits supplement the unchanged host validation metric; embedding alignment alone should not imply collapse or diversity loss.
